column1: T2 cumulative emissions against cumulative reported supply
column2: a bank cannot emit gas that was never supplied: cumulative emissions <= cumulative supply, for any leak rate and any bank age
column3: EDGAR cumulative F-gas emissions 1990-2024 = 144.8 Mt CO2e
column4: Pakistan's REPORTED Article-7 Annex-F consumption totals 26.7 Mt CO2e across the four reported years at or before 2024 (2019, 2020, 2024); 2021-2023 are publicly unreported, and the one-stratum bounded bank's interpolated 2019-2024 supply sums to about 55.6 Mt
column5: EDGAR's cumulative emissions are 2.6x the whole interpolated Article-7-era supply
column6: NOT A CONTRADICTION ON ITS OWN - Article-7 reporting begins in 2019 and HFC supply before it is simply unreported, so a pre-2019 supply history could in principle carry the difference. What it does establish is that EDGAR's series implies a Pakistani HFC supply history several times larger than anything Pakistan has ever reported, and that difference is not evidenced anywhere in this repository.

column2: the two are independent - one accumulates imports from an empty 2012, the other counts equipment in service in 2024-25; the stock lane is HOUSEHOLDS ONLY and is a lower bound
column3: bank: supply-side 4128 t, stock-side household central 3092 t. emissions: supply-side 1.2902 Mt CO2e, stock-side 0.0009-0.0803 Mt (central 0.0121)
column4: supply-side operating loss applied to this stratum, against IPCC Table 7.9 for the matching sub-application
column6: THE DECISIVE COMPARISON. The two banks agree to within a factor of 1.3 - an import accumulation since 2012 and a 2024-25 household equipment count land on almost the same mass of refrigerant - while the EMISSIONS differ by about two orders of magnitude. With the bank size agreed, only one thing can cause that: the leak rate. The supply-side bank prices this stratum at 8 %/yr; IPCC Table 7.9 gives DOMESTIC refrigeration 0.1-0.5 %/yr and only the commercial sub-applications reach 8 %. A domestic/commercial split of this stratum - which nobody holds - decides roughly 1.2 Mt CO2e, and it is the largest single lever in the whole 2.F question.

Both of those are expected to differ: HIES counts HOUSEHOLD room units only, and offices, shops, hotels and institutions hold a large AC stock outside it, while this screen's 55 percent central HFC share (the balance HCFC-22) pushes its own bank down. The emissions ratio (9.0x) is close to the bank ratio, so unlike refrigeration the gap here is about STOCK COVERAGE and species share, not about the leak rate: 6 %/yr sits comfortably inside Table 7.9's 1-10 percent for this sub-application.
